problem.title: Capturing Tail Outliers with Tail-Based Trace Sampling
problem.prompt: A checkout platform processing 18,000 RPS uses 1% uniform head-based trace sampling to control APM ingestion costs ($14k/mo). Customers report intermittent 6-second freezes on 0.5% of orders, but APM shows almost zero slow traces because 99% of those rare outliers are dropped at the ingress gateway before the downstream lock contention even happens.
requirements: Capture 100% of traces with total duration > 1,500 ms or any span containing an HTTP 5xx / gRPC error.
Retain a 0.5% baseline sample of healthy fast traces for latency distribution baselines.
Keep APM storage/ingestion costs flat (under 1,200 spans/sec exported to backend).
Handle 18,000 RPS across 120 microservices without dropping spans due to trace-id routing mismatches.
constraints: Average trace has 12 spans (~1.8 KB per span) across Go, Java, and Python services.
Cannot exceed 32 GB RAM per collector pod; max end-to-end trace visibility lag is 45 seconds.
All services already emit OpenTelemetry OTLP/gRPC spans.

stages.learnerPrompt: Why does 1% head-based sampling fail to capture rare 0.5% tail-latency events even though 0.5% * 18,000 RPS = 90 slow requests per second?

referenceMaterial.summary: Head-based sampling decides at the ingress hop before execution begins, discarding 99% of slow requests blindly and keeping only ~0.9 slow traces/sec without bias toward anomalies.
approachSteps: Explain that trace_id sampling happens at hop 1 before DB locks or downstream timeouts occur.
Show that 99% of diagnostic traces for the 0.5% tail are dropped immediately.
Note that if a downstream service also samples independently, traces become fragmented.
referenceMaterial.codeSnippet:
# Broken head-based sampling config in app SDK
OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER: "traceidratio"
OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG: "0.01" # Blindly drops 99% of 6-second freezes
tradeOffs: Head-based sampling requires zero collector memory but provides zero anomaly prioritization.
alternatives: Debug-header triggered tracing (only works when caller knows a request will be slow).
failureModes: Missing root cause for p99.9 outages because no slow trace survived the 1% coin flip.

stages.learnerPrompt: Design the OpenTelemetry Collector configuration for Tier 1 (routing) and Tier 2 (tail sampling) to capture 100% of >1.5s traces and errors within 1,200 spans/sec.
Inspect the production Tier 1 and Tier 2 OpenTelemetry Collector YAML configs with memory_limiter, traceID loadbalancing, and tail_sampling policies.

referenceMaterial.summary: Two-tier OTel Collector config: Tier 1 exports SpanMetrics and routes by traceID; Tier 2 buffers for 30s and applies latency, error, and 0.2% probabilistic policies.
approachSteps: Configure Tier 1 loadbalancing exporter with routing_key: traceID.
Configure Tier 2 memory_limiter (12 GiB) to prevent OOMKills.
Define tail_sampling policies for status_code ERROR, latency >= 1500ms, and 0.2% baseline.
referenceMaterial.codeSnippet:
# Tier 2 Tail-Sampling Collector (otel-tail-collector.yaml)
processors:
  memory_limiter:
    check_interval: 1s
    limit_mib: 12288
    spike_limit_mib: 2048
  tail_sampling:
    decision_wait: 30s
    num_traces: 250000
    expected_new_traces_per_sec: 5000
    policies:
      - name: errors-policy
        type: status_code
        status_code: { status_codes: [ERROR] }
      - name: slow-traces-policy
        type: latency
        latency: { threshold_ms: 1500 }
      - name: baseline-sample
        type: probabilistic
        probabilistic: { sampling_percentage: 0.2 }
tradeOffs: Buffering 216k spans/sec for 30s requires ~26 GB fleet RAM across 4 stateful pods.
alternatives: Dynamic head-based adaptive sampling per endpoint (still misses per-request lock contention).
failureModes: Routing Tier 1 -> Tier 2 through a round-robin Kubernetes Service splits traces across pods.

stages.learnerPrompt: Why must we compute RED metrics (p50/p99 latency) in Tier 1 before tail sampling rather than inside the APM backend?

referenceMaterial.summary: Tail sampling intentionally over-represents slow and errored traces (100% of >1.5s vs 0.2% of fast), which severely skews any latency percentiles computed post-sampling.
approachSteps: Show the math: keeping 100% of 0.5% slow traces and 0.2% of 99.5% fast traces makes slow traces ~71% of the exported dataset.
Place spanmetrics connector in Tier 1 before loadbalancing/tail_sampling.
Export exact Prometheus histograms independently of trace sampling.
referenceMaterial.codeSnippet:
# Tier 1 SpanMetrics + TraceID LoadBalancer
connectors:
  spanmetrics:
    histogram:
      explicit:
        buckets: [10ms, 50ms, 100ms, 250ms, 500ms, 1500ms, 5000ms]
exporters:
  loadbalancing:
    routing_key: traceID
    protocol:
      otlp:
        tls: { insecure: true }
    resolver:
      dns:
        hostname: otel-tail-collector-headless.monitoring.svc.cluster.local
tradeOffs: Computing spanmetrics on 216k spans/sec adds ~15% CPU to Tier 1 gateways.
alternatives: Instrumenting Prometheus histograms directly in every microservice SDK.
failureModes: Dashboards alerting on fake 90% error rates because metrics were derived from tail-sampled traces.

stages.learnerPrompt: What happens if traffic spikes 3x to 54,000 RPS during a flash sale? How does the collector avoid OOMKill or silent span loss?

referenceMaterial.summary: A 3x spike pushes buffered payload to ~35 GB raw (~75 GB with Go overhead), exceeding 64 GB fleet RAM unless memory_limiter and attribute stripping are configured.
approachSteps: Size Tier 2 pods with 2.4x headroom (4 x 16 GB or 6 x 16 GB).
Configure memory_limiter to refuse/drop new spans cleanly instead of OOMKilling the pod and losing all 30s of buffered traces.
Strip large debug attributes (e.g., full SQL bodies > 512 bytes) at Tier 1 before buffering.
referenceMaterial.codeSnippet:
processors:
  attributes/truncate:
    actions:
      - key: db.statement
        action: delete # Strip bulky SQL payloads before 30s Tier 2 buffering
tradeOffs: Dropping bulky attributes saves ~40% RAM per span at the cost of not seeing full SQL strings in traces.
alternatives: Reducing decision_wait dynamically or spilling spans to local NVMe.
failureModes: OOMKill wipes out the entire 30s in-memory buffer of all 135,000 active traces simultaneously.

stages.learnerPrompt: How do you validate that 100% of slow traces are actually arriving complete without missing child spans?

referenceMaterial.summary: Monitor collector decision latency, orphan span rate, and exporter drop counters in Prometheus.
approachSteps: Run a synthetic canary trace every 60s with a forced 2,000ms sleep and assert all 12 spans arrive in APM.
referenceMaterial.codeSnippet:
-- PromQL alerts for Tail-Sampling health
rate(otelcol_processor_tail_sampling_sampling_trace_dropped_too_early[5m]) > 0
rate(otelcol_processor_refused_spans[1m]) > 0
tradeOffs: Synthetic 2,000 ms canary adds negligible cost (1 trace/min) while guaranteeing end-to-end pipeline verification.
failureModes: Clock skew or >30s async spans causing partial orphan traces.

spark.summary: Uniform 1% head-based sampling drops 99% of slow and errored traces before they finish, leaving engineers blind to rare p99.9 latency outliers.
spark.keyTakeaway: Switch from pure head-based probabilistic sampling to OpenTelemetry Collector tail-based sampling that buffers spans in memory for 30 s and keeps 100% of errors and high-latency traces.

problem.title: Capturing Tail Outliers with Tail-Based Trace Sampling
problem.prompt: A checkout platform processing 18,000 RPS uses 1% uniform head-based trace sampling to control APM ingestion costs ($14k/mo). Customers report intermittent 6-second freezes on 0.5% of orders, but APM shows almost zero slow traces because 99% of those rare outliers are dropped at the ingress gateway before the downstream lock contention even happens.
requirements: Capture 100% of traces with total duration > 1,500 ms or any span containing an HTTP 5xx / gRPC error.
Retain a 0.5% baseline sample of healthy fast traces for latency distribution baselines.
Keep APM storage/ingestion costs flat (under 1,200 spans/sec exported to backend).
Handle 18,000 RPS across 120 microservices without dropping spans due to trace-id routing mismatches.
constraints: Average trace has 12 spans (~1.8 KB per span) across Go, Java, and Python services.
Cannot exceed 32 GB RAM per collector pod; max end-to-end trace visibility lag is 45 seconds.
All services already emit OpenTelemetry OTLP/gRPC spans.

concept.whyItMatters: Head-based sampling makes a blind coin-flip decision at the first hop before the request executes. Rare tail-latency bugs (lock contention, cold shards, third-party timeouts) happen in 0.1%–1% of requests, meaning 99% of diagnostic evidence is discarded before the failure even occurs.
whenToUse: High-throughput systems (> 5,000 RPS) where 100% trace retention is cost-prohibitive.
Investigating rare tail-latency spikes (p99/p99.9), intermittent deadlocks, or tenant-specific failures.
Compliance or SLA workflows requiring 100% capture of failed/errored transactions.
whenNotToUse: Low-volume services (< 200 RPS) where 100% ingestion is cheaper than running a stateful tail-sampling collector tier.
Ultra-low-latency streaming pipelines where holding spans in collector memory for 30 s violates real-time alerting SLAs.
keyPoints: Tail-based sampling buffers all spans of a trace in memory for decision_wait (e.g., 30 s) and evaluates policies (latency > 1500 ms, status == ERROR, probabilistic 0.5%) only after the trace completes.
Two-tier collector architecture is mandatory: Layer 1 (Load-Balancing Exporter) hashes on trace_id to route all spans of the same trace to the exact same Layer 2 Tail-Sampling Collector.
Memory sizing follows Little's Law: 18,000 RPS * 12 spans * 1.8 KB = 388.8 MB/s * 30 s = 11.66 GB fleet-wide raw payload (~26 GB with Go/index overhead).
Always pair tail sampling with SpanMetrics Connector at Layer 1 so RED metrics (Rate, Errors, Duration) are computed over 100% of traffic before sampling.
terms: Head-Based Sampling: Decision made at the trace root (ingress) using trace_id hash or probability before downstream execution latency or errors are known.
Tail-Based Sampling: Stateful decision made at the OpenTelemetry Collector after buffering spans for decision_wait so latency, error codes, and attributes are known.
Trace-ID Consistent Hashing: Routing all spans sharing a 128-bit trace_id to the same collector instance so partial traces are not fragmented across pods.

tradeOffs.pro: Captures 100% of p99.9 outliers and errors while keeping backend ingestion volume under 2%.
tradeOffs.con: Requires a stateful collector tier with consistent trace_id hashing and ~12–20 GB of fleet RAM for the 30 s buffer.

tradeOffs.factor: Long decision_wait (30 s) vs. Short decision_wait (5 s)
tradeOffs.pro: Prevents splitting long-running traces (e.g., 10 s checkout calls) into incomplete fragments.
tradeOffs.con: Multiplies collector memory footprint linearly (6x more RAM for 30 s vs 5 s).

failureModes.name: Split-Brain Trace Fragmentation
failureModes.description: Round-robin load balancing in front of tail-sampling collectors sends spans of the same trace to different pods, causing missed latency policies.
failureModes.mitigation: Deploy a stateless OTel Gateway tier using the loadbalancing exporter with routing_key: traceID.

failureModes.name: Collector OOM During Traffic Spikes
failureModes.description: A 3x burst triples buffered spans during the 30 s decision_wait, triggering Linux OOMKill and dropping all telemetry.
failureModes.mitigation: Configure memory_limiter processor (limit_mib, spike_limit_mib) and size num_traces headroom to 2.5x peak.

failureModes.name: Distorted Service Latency Metrics
failureModes.description: Computing p50/p99 metrics from tail-sampled traces inflates reported latency because slow traces are over-represented.
failureModes.mitigation: Run the OTel spanmetrics connector upstream of tail_sampling so metrics reflect 100% of unsampled spans.

commonMistakes: Computing Prometheus latency histograms from sampled traces instead of unsampled spans.
Forgetting traceID consistent hashing in front of tail-sampling collectors.
Setting decision_wait shorter than the p99.9 request timeout, which drops the root span before it arrives.
Leaving debug/verbose payload attributes on spans in the collector buffer, inflating RAM usage by 4x.

sections.content:
## The Problem: Head-Based Sampling Blindness

At **18,000 RPS**, uniform 1% head-based sampling drops **99% of traces at the API gateway**. When 0.5% of checkouts (`90 RPS`) hit a 6-second database lock or third-party payment stall, `89.1` of those slow traces per second are never recorded. Worse, the remaining `0.9` traces/sec are drowned out or lack upstream context, leaving engineers unable to diagnose which downstream shard caused the freeze.

## Requirements & Constraints

- **100% Outlier Capture**: Keep every trace with `latency > 1,500 ms` or `status == ERROR`.
- **Baseline Visibility**: Keep `0.5%` of fast healthy traces for normal path comparison.
- **Cost Cap**: Export `<= 1,200 spans/sec` to the APM vendor.
- **Resource Budget**: Max `32 GB RAM` per collector pod; max `45 s` trace arrival lag.

## Memory & Bandwidth Sizing

- **Incoming Span Rate**: `18,000 RPS * 12 spans/trace = 216,000 spans/sec`.
- **Raw Ingestion Bandwidth**: `216,000 * 1.8 KB = 388.8 MB/s`.
- **30-Second Buffer Footprint**: `388.8 MB/s * 30 s = 11.66 GB` raw payload. With Go heap & OTel internal index overhead (~2.2x), fleet RAM needed is `~26 GB`.
- **Collector Sizing**: Deploy **4 stateful Tail-Sampling pods** with `16 GB RAM` each (`64 GB` total = `2.4x` burst headroom). Each pod handles `4,500 traces/sec` (`135,000` active traces in its 30 s window).
- **Exported Span Rate**: `0.2%` baseline (`432 spans/sec`) + outliers (`~600 spans/sec`) = `~1,032 spans/sec` (under the `1,200` cap).

edges.label: OTLP/gRPC 100%

edges.label: 100% RED Metrics
edges.title: Compute Exact SpanMetrics
edges.description: Tier 1 computes unbiased p50/p99 histograms over 100% of spans before any trace is dropped.

edges.label: Consistent Hash(traceID)
edges.title: Route by Trace ID
edges.description: Load-balancing exporter hashes traceID so all 12 spans of a trace land on the same Tier 2 pod.

edges.label: Wait 30s & Evaluate
edges.title: Tail Policy Evaluation
edges.description: After decision_wait=30s, Tier 2 keeps traces with latency > 1500ms, error=true, or 0.2% baseline.

edges.title: Cost-Bounded APM Export
edges.description: 100% of rare 6-second freezes are exported while staying under the $14k/mo span budget.

data.caption: Separating metric generation (Tier 1) from consistent-hashed tail sampling (Tier 2) eliminates sampling bias without distorting metrics or blowing up APM costs.

sections.content:
## Detailed Design: Two-Tier OTel Collector Pipeline

1. **Disable Head Sampling in SDKs**: Set `OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER=always_on` so every microservice emits spans to the local node agent / Tier 1 gateway.
2. **Tier 1 Stateless Gateway**: Runs `spanmetrics` connector to generate exact Prometheus histograms, then uses `loadbalancing` exporter (`routing_key: traceID`) to hash spans to Tier 2.
3. **Tier 2 Stateful Tail-Sampling Pool**: Runs `memory_limiter` (`limit_mib: 12288`) followed by `tail_sampling` with `decision_wait: 30s`, `num_traces: 250000`, and 3 policies: `errors`, `latency > 1500ms`, and `probabilistic: 0.2%`.

## Failure Handling & Edge Cases

- **Tier 2 Pod Restart / Autoscaling**: Consistent hash ring reshuffles ~25% of in-flight traces during scale events, briefly splitting traces for 30 s. Use a `StatefulSet` with fixed replica count (`4` or `6`) rather than aggressive HPA.
- **Long-Running Async Jobs**: Batch jobs > 30 s may split across `decision_wait`. Exclude async queue workers via `not_in` attribute or attach explicit `sampling.priority=1`.

## Production Resolution Summary

Replace 1% head-based sampling with a **two-tier OpenTelemetry Collector** pipeline: Tier 1 computes exact RED metrics and hashes on `traceID`; Tier 2 (4x 16 GB pods) buffers for `30s` and exports 100% of `>1,500 ms` outliers and errors plus `0.2%` baseline traces, staying under `1,200 spans/sec`.
